ngcc.openQuestionAnswered: spike-A open question (1): where does the ngcc properties override live in a real cell?
ngcc.answer: NOWHERE. No override is required under a CLI-driven build. The Angular CLI does not use ngcc’s standalone default property order; it passes webpack’s resolve.mainFields as --properties, which for a browser build is [es2015, browser, module, main]. That order already places `module` ahead of `main`, which is exactly what the spike achieved by hand with `ngcc -p module main`. The spike’s failure mode is an artifact of invoking ngcc standalone, where DEFAULT_PROPERTIES_TO_CONSIDER puts `main` first.
answerProvenance: node_modules/@angular-devkit/build-angular/src/webpack/utils/helpers.js:290-297 - getMainFieldsAndConditionNames() returns [es2015, browser, module, main] for a browser build (es2020 unshifted when target >= ES2020)
ngcc.ngccConfigJsFinding: A project-root ngcc.config.js IS honoured on this path - ngcc_processor.js:80 reads <projectRoot>/ngcc.config.js and folds its bytes into the run-hash that decides whether to skip an ngcc pass. So the file is the right home for an override IF one is ever needed. For this closure it is not, so it is committed disabled as ngcc.config.js.held rather than left in place pretending to be load-bearing.

notEstablished: This proves COMPILE-AT-CELL only. It does not establish a migration. No migration was performed by the engine; the three source edits were applied by hand as a measurement of what a migration would have to do.
It does not establish runtime behaviour. Nothing was bundled, served, loaded in a browser, or executed. `ngc` emitted 121 JS files; not one of them was run.
It does not establish the witness. No holdout witness was run, and this record does not retry, weaken, or touch the sealed pigallery2 RED at the Angular 16 cell, which stands as published.

It does not establish a full `ng build`. The CLI’s ngcc invocation was reproduced verbatim from @ngtools/webpack’s own source and executed, but no webpack browser build was run end to end. pigallery2’s AppModule uses a `require('raw-loader!...')` translations factory and its angular.json styles reference bootstrap and open-iconic, neither installed here - those are bundler-stage concerns this unit did not price.
It does not establish the test or e2e closure. tsconfig.13cell.json excludes frontend/test.ts and **/*.spec.ts; the karma/protractor closure at the cell is unmeasured.
It does not establish the backend. pigallery2 is a full-stack app; only frontend/ and common/ were compiled. The backend TypeScript, typeorm 0.2.18, sqlite3 4.0.9 and the gulp build were not touched.

It does not establish that the repinned supporting libraries (ngx-bootstrap 8, ngx-toastr 14.3, ngx-clipboard 15.1) are behaviour-compatible with the Angular-8-era versions pigallery2 declares. They type-check and their directives resolve; nothing more is claimed.

It does not establish the fullTemplateTypeCheck story. The strict reading was taken at an intermediate state and shows private-member template bindings that would need work; the clean-state strict count is unmeasured.
It does not establish anything about Node eras other than 16.20.2, nor about the Angular 12.2.17 fallback cell, which this unit did not re-run.
It changes no engine claim, no support boundary and no freeze. No packages/** file was read into or written by this unit.

answersToSpikeOpenQuestions.openQuestion1-ngccOverrideLocation: ANSWERED. No override is needed on the CLI path: @ngtools/webpack passes webpack resolve.mainFields ([es2015, browser, module, main]) as ngcc --properties, which already prefers `module` over `main`. The spike’s `-p module main` was a hand reproduction of the CLI default, not a deviation from it. A project-root ngcc.config.js IS the honoured home should an override ever be needed (ngcc_processor.js reads it into its run-hash), and one is committed disabled at .versionless/work/angular-pigallery2/13cell/ngcc.config.js.held as the counterfactual. T001’s "1-2 units to plumb the ngcc override" can be released.
answersToSpikeOpenQuestions.openQuestion2-appCompiles: ANSWERED YES, at a price of three mechanical source edits. pigallery2 1.7.0’s frontend AOT-compiles at Angular 13.4.0 / Node 16.20.2 / rxjs 6.6.7 with exit 0, zero diagnostics and 121 emitted files. The four legacy libraries are not the obstacle; the obstacle was three ordinary Angular-9-era migration items, two of which have official codemods.
answersToSpikeOpenQuestions.openQuestion3-rxjs6Viability: ANSWERED for this closure. rxjs stayed at 6.6.7 throughout and nothing in the migrated pigallery2 tree demanded rxjs 7. One addition was needed: rxjs-compat@6.6.7, because the app deep-imports rxjs/Observable - which pigallery2 1.7.0 already declared. The Angular 12 fallback cell is not needed on rxjs grounds.
answersToSpikeOpenQuestions.openQuestion4-fleetPrevalence: PARTIALLY MOVED, in the unhelpful direction. This closure contains FOUR ViewEngine/legacy Angular libraries, not the three the sealed receipt names - @ngx-translate/i18n-polyfill@1.0.0 was invisible until the full application closure was installed. The fourth was consumable, but it is evidence that per-app legacy-library counts read off a receipt are floors, not totals.
